name: CorrelationPro
description: A self-contained, browser-based platform for correlation analysis of every kind, with its theory. It reads spreadsheets, CSV, TSV and pasted text with its own reader; records the kind and role of each column; checks the assumptions of each pair and recommends a coefficient; computes every coefficient for two variables with exact, asymptotic or permutation tests, analytic and bootstrap intervals and the Bayes factor; builds correlation matrices with multiple-testing corrections, the nearest positive-definite matrix, shrinkage, KMO and nine glyphs for up to a thousand variables; measures nonlinear dependence (dCor, HSIC, MIC, xi, tau*, Hoeffding's D, mutual information, maximal correlation) and fits five copula families; computes partial, semipartial, multiple and canonical correlation, RV, Procrustes, co-inertia and Mantel; categorical, ordinal and latent correlations and the heterogeneous matrix; agreement and reliability (CCC, Bland-Altman, six ICC forms, kappas, Kendall's W, Krippendorff's alpha, Gwet's AC1/AC2); correlation in data with structure (groups and Simpson's paradox, repeated measures, time series, spatial data, phylogenetic contrasts, circular and compositional data); correlation networks; and compares correlations and matrices, corrects for attenuation and range restriction, plans power and sample size and combines correlations by meta-analysis. It ends in publication figures, colour-vision-safe palettes, a correlation table and a methods section written from what was actually run. Spanish and English interface. Every engine of Blocks 1 to 12 was checked against independent implementations in R: 19,334 comparisons with no disagreement.
softwareRequirements: A modern web browser; no installation
